idea-plugin.name: Nest Switch
idea-plugin.description:
Jumping around a NestJS module means hunting through the project tree: the controller is next to the service, but the DTOs are in dto/, the entity is in entities/, and the spec is wherever it landed. Nest Switch puts the whole module one keystroke away.

Press Ctrl+Alt+Home (⌃⌘↑ on macOS), or Navigate → Related Symbol…, from any file in a Nest module, and the standard platform popup lists every file of that module, grouped by role. Type to filter, Enter to open, Shift+Enter to open in a split.

What counts as "the module"

The nearest folder above the current file that declares a *.module.ts. Every .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx file beneath it is listed — sub-folders included — so dto/create-user.dto.ts and entities/user.entity.ts show up alongside the controller and service. Nested modules keep their own scope: a sub-folder with its own *.module.ts is left out, so a parent module never swallows its children.

Grouped by role, not dumped in a list

Items are sorted into sections — Module, Controllers, Services, Resolvers, Gateways, Providers, Repositories, Entities, Schemas, DTOs, Interfaces, Guards, Strategies, Interceptors, Pipes, Middleware, Filters, Decorators, Mappers, Listeners, Tasks, Events, Tests, and more. The role comes from the file name (create-user.dto.ts → DTOs); when the name carries no role, the sub-folder names the section (entities/ → Entities). Files in sub-folders are labelled with their path, so dto/create-user.dto.ts is never ambiguous.

Quiet by design

  • No icons, no gutter markers, no inlay hints — nothing is added to your editor.
  • Inert outside Nest — silent unless the project actually depends on @nestjs/*.
  • Nothing to configure — no settings page, no setup.
  • Every JetBrains IDE, 2023.3+ — core platform APIs only, so Community editions work too, with no dependency on the JavaScript/TypeScript plugin.
